findings.statement: CA9 is rank 1 in the convergence ranking (score 4.5197). Open Targets association score 0.3088, rank 79 of 1998. Drugs returned: GIRENTUXIMAB (PHASE_3), IODINE I 124 GIRENTUXIMAB (PHASE_2), SULTHIAME (PHASE_4), ETHOXZOLAMIDE (WITHDRAWAL). UniProt location is cell membrane (microvillus membrane), so it is accessible to antibodies and radioligands and measurable as a biomarker. Tumour RNA log2FC is 6.312 and protein log2FC is 2.269. DepMap shows no ccRCC dependency (mean effect 0.051, 0.0 of lines dependent), so CA9 is a targeting handle (antibody or imaging) and not a functional dependency.

CD70 is rank 3 in the convergence ranking (score 4.2143). Open Targets association score 0.0572. Drugs returned: CUSATUZUMAB (PHASE_2), VORSETUZUMAB (PHASE_1), VORSETUZUMAB MAFODOTIN (PHASE_1), MDX-1411 (PHASE_1). UniProt location is plasma membrane, which suits antibody, ADC or CAR-T approaches. Tumour RNA log2FC is 4.464 and protein log2FC is 2.421. It is not a DepMap dependency (mean effect 0.251), so the case rests on surface expression and not on tumour dependency.

ENPP3 is rank 29 in the convergence ranking. It is tumour-up at RNA (log2FC 3.895) and protein (log2FC 1.544). The antibody-drug conjugate AGS-16C3F is at PHASE_2. UniProt location is apical cell membrane and secreted. Open Targets association score is only 0.0356, and DepMap shows no dependency (mean effect 0.091). This is a tractable, surface-accessible but clinically weakly validated antigen.

EPAS1 (HIF-2alpha) is the established ccRCC drug target. BELZUTIFAN is at APPROVAL. Open Targets association score 0.4871, and it is the 9th-ranked ccRCC target in the top-25 list. It is the only candidate with a selective DepMap signal: ccRCC mean effect -0.143 versus 0.157 in other lines, selectivity 0.3, 0.208 of ccRCC lines dependent, padj 0.061, not common essential. Reactome pathways include regulation of gene expression by Hypoxia-inducible Factor. Convergence rank is 38, because its RNA is only mildly up while the drug acts on the protein. It validates the pipeline's dependency layer.

VHL is the founding ccRCC driver. Open Targets association score 0.6466, the top-ranked ccRCC association. It is somatically mutated in 247 of 511 tumours (freq 0.483, padj 0.0, recurrent). It has no drugs in the convergence ranking. It is a loss-of-function tumour suppressor, so the actionable route is the downstream HIF-2alpha axis (EPAS1/belzutifan), not VHL itself.

PBRM1 is the second-ranked Open Targets ccRCC association (score 0.6348). It is mutated in 185 of 511 tumours (freq 0.362, padj 4.59e-239, recurrent). It is a tumour-suppressor driver with association evidence only and no established drug. It is relevant as a stratification marker, not as a direct target.

NNMT is rank 7 in the convergence ranking (score 3.9643) and has the highest biomarker-profile score among the top genes. It is tumour-up (RNA log2FC 4.67, protein log2FC 2.709). It is cytoplasmic (UniProt), so it is not an antibody target. No drugs are returned. Open Targets association score is 0.0598. Higher expression is associated with worse prognosis in TCGA (Cox log HR 0.301). DepMap shows no dependency (mean effect 0.316), so it is a metabolic-epigenetic biomarker candidate and a small-molecule tractability hypothesis only.

SLC16A3 (MCT4) is rank 15 in the convergence ranking and is tumour-up (RNA log2FC 3.435, protein log2FC 2.279). Open Targets association score is 0.0491 and no drugs are returned. Predicted tractability is high, but there is no DepMap dependency in ccRCC (mean effect -0.015). It is an untested, tractable-by-prediction candidate.

SCARB1 is rank 5 in the convergence ranking (score 4.1052) and has the highest target-profile score among the top five (4.1314). It is tumour-up (RNA log2FC 2.974, protein log2FC 1.837). Open Targets association score is 0.4049 with a genetic-association component of 0.519. No drugs are returned, and there is no DepMap dependency (mean effect 0.002). This is an association-plus-expression candidate with no clinical drug.

ALDOB is rank 2 in the convergence ranking (score 4.2206) and is a biomarker candidate (biomarker profile 4.3755). It is down in tumour (RNA log2FC -7.028, protein log2FC -2.273). Higher expression is associated with better survival (Cox log HR -0.358, padj 0.000023). Open Targets association score is 0.0701. No drugs are returned, and there is no DepMap dependency (mean effect 0.156). Loss of this proximal-tubule marker is a diagnostic or prognostic readout, not a target.

SLC22A8 is rank 4 in the convergence ranking (score 4.1667). It is strongly down in tumour (RNA log2FC -6.715, protein log2FC -2.264), and higher expression is associated with better survival (Cox log HR -0.402). Drugs returned: PROBENECID (PHASE_4) and PRATOSARTAN (PHASE_3), which are not ccRCC-directed. Open Targets association score is 0.0662. This is a loss-of-expression biomarker, not a target.

MTOR is an established ccRCC drug target (Open Targets association score 0.525, 6th in the top-25 list) and is a clinical-standard pathway. It does not appear in the top 40 of the convergence ranking, so omics convergence does not single it out. It is kept as a reference established target.

caveats: The strongest omics-convergent genes (CA9, CD70, NNMT, ENPP3, SLC16A3, SCARB1) show no DepMap dependency in ccRCC lines, so druggability here rests on surface expression and not on tumour dependency. EPAS1 is the only one with a selective dependency signal (padj 0.061, not significant at 0.05).

Many top-ranked genes are down-regulated proximal-tubule markers (ALDOB, SLC22A8, UMOD and others). They are biomarkers of lost tissue identity, and tumour purity or cell-of-origin confounding cannot be excluded.

Open Targets scores are literature and genetics weighted, and some convergence-ranking drug records (for example sulthiame, probenecid) are not ccRCC-directed. Only drug stages as returned are reported.

STRING interactions and CD70/CA9 mutation recurrence were not queried, to stay within the tool budget. CA9 DepMap returned no evidence id, so its dependency values are not citable beyond the ranking row.
